messages:
anya: quick thread — ran NTK/YARN sweep targeting RoPE scale 1.0→2.0 on mixtral-8x and mistral-7b, longctx 8k.

ravi: what triggered this? perf reg or quality drift?

anya: saw perplexity jump and hallucination rate increase for mixtral when scale >1.6; also kernel selector moved from fast-attn -> fallback kernel under certain kv-shape combos.

cheng: can you paste the repro command + perf snippet?

anya: sure
```
./scripts/ropexp/run.sh --model mixtral-8x --rope ntk --scale 1.8 --ctx 8192 --batch 8 --kv-config head-slice-64
```
```
perf summary (p50/p95 latency tokens/sec):
model mixtral-8x scale=1.8 ctx=8192 batch=8 -> p50=42ms p95=290ms tokens/s=320
fallback kernel enabled at step ~1200
perplexity dev-set: 12.4 -> 18.9 (baseline 11.7)
```

sam: fallback kernel? which condition flipped the selector?

anya: selector log shows 'kv-layout mismatch' for head-slice combo + continuous batching spike. Basically routing heuristic saw >3x variance in seq-len and forced aligned kernel -> costlier path.

ravi: hmm. did we hit the head-dim / kv-dim boundary? mixtral has 128 head_kv, right?

cheng: mixtral-8x head_kv=64? need to double-check. Could be kv-pad rounding in kernel lookup.

anya: mixtral-8x config: heads=32 head_kv=64 (total kv_dim=2048). The selector uses threshold 2048->switch. When we applied head-slice-64 it created padding to 2304 -> triggers fallback.

perf-bot: auto-profile uploaded: https://staging-perf/reports/2140077777

sam: can we add a temporary rule: allow kernel match on padded_kv within 12%? to avoid churn

ravi: cautious — that might mask real incompatibilities. Better: prefer flexible kernel that handles padded shapes but record a perf delta and fall back after N samples.

anya: proposal: 1) relax selector epsilon for kv padding up to 12% 2) add a micro-benchmark invocation in runtime cold-start that verifies fast-attn correctness for the padded shape 3) add a quality guard: if perplexity rises >20% vs baseline, rollback config.

cheng: also add a small kv-cache test in the eval harness — I saw evictions cause different kv-shape exposures over longctx.

anya: yes, longctx churn exposes slice alignment. I also observed continuous batching creates transient shapes: seqs of 256 -> 4096 mixed in same batch.

sam: can we reproduce with deterministic single-batch test? I can run a controlled trace tomorrow.

anya: i'll push a PR with the selector epsilon + extra micro-bench. also adding telemetry for 'selector_reason' and 'padded_kv_size'.

ravi: link when ready. we should gate the change behind a canary on dedicated cluster.

perf-bot: canary run queued for cluster-dedicated-3, will post metrics once done.

anya: action items: @sam run deterministic repro; @cheng add kv-cache eviction test to eval harness; @ravi review selector PR; I'll monitor canary and the perf/quality dashboard.

sam: noted, starting repro now.

ravi: heading to standup, ping me on PR.

anya: thanks team :thumbsup:

perf-bot: report (quick): canary p50 delta +3ms, p95 +25ms, perplexity delta -1.2% (prelim)

sam: nice, keep watching for mixtral-specific cliffs.

anya: updated the run script to include --trace-selector true if anyone wants deeper logs.

cheng: good. also add a short note in the release notes: 'kernel selector tuning: relaxed kv padding epsilon, added micro-benchmark and selector telemetry'

anya: will draft and tag @product-infra for visibility.
